main_competence_name: Demonstrate mastery of the history of sports and its importance
specific_competence_name: Demonstrate an understanding of the history and development of sports in Tanzania
learning_activity_name: Explain the historical development of sports in Tanzania from international and national perspectives (development, spread and impacts)
sla_name: History and Development of Sports in Tanzania
sla_assessment_criteria: The historical development of sports in Tanzania from international and national are well explained.
sla_teaching_aids: Newspaper|Magazine|Sport documentary videos|Sport sessions in television|Radio
sla_references: TET(2023), SPORT STUDIES SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION FORM V-VI, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Sport has developed in Tanzania from traditional games and physical skills of communities into organised national and international competition. Understanding this history explains how sport spread and what it has meant for the nation.
sla_notes_details: Before colonial rule, communities practised wrestling, running, hunting games, dances, ball games and stick games as part of rites, training for defence and entertainment. Colonial missionaries, administrators and schools introduced football, athletics, netball, cricket and boxing and organised them in schools and clubs. After independence in 1961 the government created bodies such as the National Sports Council (now Baraza la Michezo la Taifa), sports associations and school competitions (UMISETA and UMITASHUMTA), and Tanzania joined the Olympic, Commonwealth and All-Africa Games, where athletes such as Filbert Bayi and Suleiman Nyambui won medals in the 1970s and 1980s. Development can be discussed under three headings: development (from traditional games to organised sport), spread (schools, clubs, media, migration and international contacts) and impacts (health, unity, employment, national identity and international recognition).
sla_notes_illustrations: Tracing football: it was introduced by colonial administrators and missionaries, spread through schools and towns, produced clubs such as Simba and Young Africans, and today feeds national teams like Taifa Stars, showing development, spread and impact in one sport.
sla_notes_daily_life: Every school sports day, community football tournament and national team match a family watches on television is a living result of the historical development of sports in Tanzania.
sla_exercise: Name two traditional physical activities practised in Tanzanian communities before colonial rule.::Wrestling and running (also stick games or dances).||Which school competitions promote sport in Tanzania?::UMITASHUMTA for primary schools and UMISETA for secondary schools.||State two impacts of sports on Tanzanian society.::Promotion of health and national unity (also employment and international recognition).

main_competence_name: Demonstrate mastery of the relationship between human physiology and performance in sports
specific_competence_name: Demonstrate a basic understanding of the structure and functions of the human body systems
learning_activity_name: Describe the structure and functions of human body systems that relate to physical exercises and sports (musculoskeletal, cardiovascular, respiratory, nervous, endocrine and digestive systems)
sla_name: Structure and Functions of Human Body Systems in Sports
sla_assessment_criteria: The structures and functions of human body systems related to physical exercises and sports are well described.
sla_references: TET(2023), SPORT STUDIES SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION FORM V-VI, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: The body systems work together to produce and control movement during exercise. Sports students must know the structure and function of each system that supports performance.
sla_notes_details: The musculoskeletal system consists of bones, joints and muscles: bones give shape and protection, joints allow movement and skeletal muscles contract to pull on bones. The cardiovascular system (heart, blood vessels, blood) transports oxygen, nutrients and wastes; the respiratory system (nose, trachea, bronchi, lungs, alveoli) exchanges oxygen and carbon dioxide. The nervous system (brain, spinal cord, nerves) coordinates movement and reaction, the endocrine system releases hormones such as adrenaline and insulin that regulate energy and stress, and the digestive system breaks food into glucose, amino acids and fatty acids that fuel and repair the body. During exercise heart rate, breathing rate and blood flow to working muscles all rise.
sla_notes_illustrations: During a 100 m sprint the brain sends signals through nerves to leg muscles, the heart pumps more blood, the lungs supply more oxygen and adrenaline is released; the digestive system supplied the glucose stored earlier as glycogen.
sla_notes_daily_life: Knowing how the body systems work helps an athlete understand why breathing becomes faster during a football match and why a good meal before training gives energy.
sla_exercise: Name the three main parts of the musculoskeletal system.::Bones, joints and muscles.||What is the function of the respiratory system in sport?::It supplies oxygen to the blood and removes carbon dioxide.||Which system releases adrenaline during exercise?::The endocrine system.

main_competence_name: Demonstrate mastery of the relationship between human physiology and performance in sports
specific_competence_name: Demonstrate a basic understanding of the role of human body systems and movements in sports
learning_activity_name: Apply the knowledge of various body systems (musculoskeletal, cardiovascular, respiratory, nervous, endocrine and digestive systems) to enhance performance in physical exercises and selected sports: Athletics (running, throwing and jumping), swimming, football, netball, basketball, table tennis, tennis volleyball and handball
sla_name: Applying Knowledge of Body Systems to Performance
sla_assessment_criteria: Knowledge of skeletal, muscular, circulatory, respiratory, nervous, digestive and endocrine systems are well applied in physical exercises and selected sports.
sla_references: TET(2023), SPORT STUDIES SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION FORM V-VI, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Knowledge of body systems is used to improve movement, endurance, strength and safety in exercises and selected sports. Students learn by observing demonstrations and then practising.
sla_notes_details: Musculoskeletal knowledge is applied by warming up muscles and joints, using correct posture and technique in running, throwing, jumping, swimming, football, netball, basketball, table tennis, tennis, volleyball and handball. Cardiovascular and respiratory knowledge guides endurance training such as continuous running and controlled breathing rhythms in swimming. Nervous system knowledge improves reaction time and coordination through drills, the endocrine system explains stress control and energy release before competition, and the digestive system guides pre- and post-training nutrition and hydration. Performance improves when training loads match what each system can adapt to.
sla_notes_illustrations: A long jumper applies body-system knowledge by warming up the leg muscles, using a fast run-up (nervous and muscular coordination), breathing deeply before the approach and eating a light carbohydrate meal two hours earlier.
sla_notes_daily_life: A person who understands the body systems can plan a safe fitness routine, avoid injuries and enjoy exercise for better health throughout life.
sla_exercise: Why should an athlete warm up before playing?::To prepare muscles, joints, heart and lungs and reduce injuries.||Which body system is mainly trained by continuous running?::The cardiovascular and respiratory systems.||How does the digestive system support performance?::It provides glucose and nutrients from food that supply energy and repair tissues.

learning_activity_name: Describe principles of training in sports (specificity, overload, progression, variety, recovery, individuality and consistency)
sla_assessment_criteria: Principles of training in sports and exercises are well described.
sla_references: TET(2023), SPORT STUDIES SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION FORM V-VI, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Principles of training are rules that guide coaches and athletes to plan training that is effective and safe. They ensure that the body adapts and improves without injury.
sla_notes_details: Specificity means training must match the demands of the sport, such as sprint work for sprinters. Overload means working harder than normal, by increasing frequency, intensity, time or type (FITT). Progression means increasing the load gradually, variety avoids boredom by changing drills, recovery gives the body time to repair and adapt, individuality means programmes suit each athlete's age, sex, fitness and goals, and consistency means training regularly over a long period because gains are lost when training stops (reversibility).
sla_notes_illustrations: A netball coach begins with three sessions a week of 30 minutes (overload), adds five minutes each week (progression), varies drills between shooting and passing (variety) and gives a rest day after two hard sessions (recovery).
sla_notes_daily_life: A person who starts jogging for health should follow the same principles: begin gently, increase slowly, rest enough and keep going regularly.
sla_exercise: What is the principle of overload?::Training harder than the body is used to so that it adapts.||Why is recovery important in training?::It allows the body to repair and adapt, preventing injury and overtraining.||Give an example of specificity for a swimmer.::Doing swimming drills and laps rather than only running.

learning_activity_name: Apply principles of training in selected sports: Athletics (running, throwing and jumping), swimming, football and netball
sla_name: Applying Principles of Training in Athletics, Swimming, Football and Netball
sla_assessment_criteria: Principles of training in selected sports: Athletics (running, throwing and jumping), swimming, football and netball are well applied.
sla_references: TET(2023), SPORT STUDIES SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION FORM V-VI, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Principles of training are applied by designing and performing suitable drills in the selected sports. Students demonstrate how each principle appears in real practice.
sla_notes_details: In athletics, specificity is shown by sprint starts for sprinters and run-up drills for jumpers, and progression by lengthening distances or adding hurdles. In swimming, overload is applied by adding laps or reducing rest between sets, and variety by mixing strokes. In football, small-sided games, passing circuits and shuttle runs train specificity, and progression increases the pressure of defenders. In netball, footwork, passing and shooting drills are made harder by adding time limits or opponents. Each session should include warm-up, main part, cool-down and rest, and record keeping supports individuality and consistency.
sla_notes_illustrations: A football coach plans a passing drill: first in pairs without opponents, then with one defender, then in a four-against-two game, showing progression while keeping the drill specific to match play.
sla_notes_daily_life: Community coaches, school sports teachers and athletes use the same steps to prepare teams for tournaments and to keep fit through the year.
sla_exercise: How can a swimmer apply overload?::By increasing the number of laps or reducing rest time between sets.||Give an example of progression in football training.::Moving from passing without opponents to passing against defenders.||Which part of a training session reduces stiffness after exercise?::The cool-down.

specific_competence_name: Develop advanced skills in selected sports
learning_activity_name: Perform advanced tactics and drills in selected sports (principles, systems and styles of play)
sla_name: Advanced Tactics and Drills in Selected Sports
sla_assessment_criteria: Advanced tactics and drills in selected sports are well performed.
sla_references: TET(2023), SPORT STUDIES SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION FORM V-VI, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Advanced tactics and drills prepare players to work as a team and to respond to opponents in competition. They build on basic skills learnt earlier.
sla_notes_details: Tactics are plans of play, such as attacking and defensive systems (for example 4-4-2 in football, zone and player-to-player defence in netball and basketball). Principles of play include creating space, keeping possession, supporting the player with the ball, and balance between attack and defence. Systems are the organised shapes of a team and styles of play are the way a team plays, for instance fast counter-attack or slow build-up. Drills such as passing triangles, pick-and-roll practice, pressing exercises and set-piece routines are repeated with increasing pressure until they are automatic. Coaches use whistles, cones and balls and give feedback after each drill.
sla_notes_illustrations: A team practises a counter-attack drill: after winning the ball, the defender passes to the midfielder, who sends a long pass to a winger running into open space, and the exercise is repeated with a defender added.
sla_notes_daily_life: The same tactical thinking is used in community leagues where teams plan their formations and roles before each match.
sla_exercise: What is a tactic in sports?::A planned way of playing to gain an advantage over opponents.||Give an example of a principle of play.::Creating space or supporting the player with the ball.||Why are drills repeated many times?::So that skills become automatic under pressure.

specific_competence_name: Develop advanced skills in selected sports
learning_activity_name: Play by observing rules and regulations governing selected sports: Athletics (running, throwing and jumping), swimming, football and netball
sla_name: Playing by the Rules of Athletics, Swimming, Football and Netball
sla_assessment_criteria: Rules and regulations are well observed in playing selected sports Athletics (running, throwing and jumping), swimming, football and netball.
sla_references: TET(2023), SPORT STUDIES SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION FORM V-VI, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Every sport has rules and regulations that make the game fair, safe and enjoyable. Students practise by playing while observing them.
sla_notes_details: In athletics, rules cover false starts, lanes, legal throws and the number of jumping attempts. In swimming, rules cover stroke technique, turns, starts and disqualification for illegal strokes. Football rules (the Laws of the Game) cover the offside rule, fouls, free kicks, penalties and the roles of the referee and assistants. In netball, players must respect court areas, footwork rules, passing time limits and contact rules. Peer teaching is used so that students observe each other, point out errors and help to apply the rules correctly. Fair play, respect for officials and team discipline are also observed.
sla_notes_illustrations: In a school match a player takes a throw-in with a foot off the line and a classmate acting as referee awards the throw to the other team, after which the group discusses the rule.
sla_notes_daily_life: Knowing rules helps citizens to referee local matches, avoid disputes, respect laws in society and enjoy sports as spectators.
sla_exercise: What is a false start in athletics?::Leaving the starting block before the starting signal.||Give one basic rule of netball.::A player holding the ball must not move with it beyond the footwork rule (or must pass within three seconds).||Why are rules needed in sport?::To ensure fairness, safety and order.

main_competence_name: Demonstrate mastery of the basic principles of sports management and administration
specific_competence_name: Demonstrate an understanding of basic principles of leadership, administration and management in sports
learning_activity_name: Describe the principles of sports management, leadership and administration (theories, skills and functions)
sla_name: Principles of Sports Management, Leadership and Administration
sla_assessment_criteria: The principles of sport management, leadership and administration are well described.
sla_teaching_aids: Newspaper|Magazine|Sports documentary videos|Sport sessions in television|Radio
sla_references: TET(2023), SPORT STUDIES SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION FORM V-VI, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Managing sport means planning, organising and controlling people and resources so that teams and events succeed. Leadership and administration provide direction and order.
sla_notes_details: Management theories include the classical (scientific and administrative) theories, human relations theories and modern systems and contingency theories, which explain how work should be organised and how leaders should motivate people. Skills needed include communication, decision-making, planning, financial control, conflict management and teamwork. The main functions of sports management are planning, organising, staffing, directing and controlling (with budgeting and coordinating). Administration deals with records, rules, finance and meetings, while leadership guides and inspires athletes and officials.
sla_notes_illustrations: A school sports master planning a tournament sets dates and budget (planning), forms committees for fields, referees and refreshments (organising and staffing), guides the teams during the event (directing) and checks results and finances afterwards (controlling).
sla_notes_daily_life: The same skills are used to run a village football league, a club or any community project.
sla_exercise: List two functions of sports management.::Planning and organising (also staffing, directing, controlling).||Name two skills a sports manager needs.::Communication and decision-making.||What is the difference between leadership and administration?::Leadership guides and motivates people while administration deals with records, rules and resources.

main_competence_name: Demonstrate mastery of the basic principles of sports management and administration
specific_competence_name: Demonstrate an understanding of basic principles of leadership, administration and management in sports
learning_activity_name: Describe the leadership, administrative and managerial structures of sport organisations
sla_name: Leadership, Administrative and Managerial Structures of Sport Organisations
sla_assessment_criteria: The leadership, administrative and managerial structures of sport organizations are well described.
sla_teaching_aids: Newspaper|Magazine|Sports documentary videos|Sport sessions in television|Radio
sla_references: TET(2023), SPORT STUDIES SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION FORM V-VI, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Sport organisations have structured positions and levels of authority. Students study these structures through simulation of real organisations.
sla_notes_details: In Tanzania sport is organised from school and community levels up to national and international bodies: the Ministry responsible for sports, the National Sports Council, national federations and associations (for example the Tanzania Football Federation, Tanzania Olympic Committee and Athletics Tanzania), regional and district associations and clubs. A typical structure has a general assembly, an executive committee, a chairperson, secretary, treasurer, coaches, technical and medical staff and referees. Leaders make policy, managers implement it and administrators keep records and finance. International links include CAF, FIFA and the International Olympic Committee.
sla_notes_illustrations: In a role-play simulation students act as chairperson, secretary, treasurer and coach of a club and hold a meeting to pick a team for a regional tournament, then discuss the lessons learnt.
sla_notes_daily_life: Understanding these structures helps young people to join clubs, run school sports committees and start community teams.
sla_exercise: Name one national sport governing body in Tanzania.::Tanzania Football Federation (or Tanzania Olympic Committee, National Sports Council).||Which officer keeps the financial records of a club?::The treasurer.||What is the role of an executive committee?::To make and implement decisions on behalf of members.

specific_competence_name: Design and conduct a project in sports
learning_activity_name: Design and execute a project in sports
sla_name: Designing and Executing a Sports Project
sla_assessment_criteria: The project in sports is well designed and executed.
sla_references: TET(2023), SPORT STUDIES SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION FORM V-VI, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: A project lets students apply what they have learnt to solve a real challenge in sports. Form Five begins the project and Form Six completes it.
sla_notes_details: Steps are identifying a sports problem (for example lack of facilities, low participation of girls or poor coaching), stating objectives, planning activities, budgeting, collecting data by observation, interviews or questionnaires, carrying out the activity, recording findings and preparing to report. Projects may include organising an inter-class tournament, training a team or building simple equipment. The teacher guides in pairs, assesses planning, implementation and teamwork, and students keep a project diary.
sla_notes_illustrations: A pair identifies that few girls join football, surveys 50 girls to find reasons, organises a girls' tournament for one week and records the increase in participation.
sla_notes_daily_life: Project skills are used in later work such as organising community events and managing small businesses.
sla_exercise: Name the first step in a sports project.::Identifying a sports problem or challenge.||Give one example of a sports project.::Organising an inter-class tournament.||Why is a project diary useful?::It records the activities and progress for reporting and assessment.

main_competence_name: Demonstrate mastery of the history of sports and its importance
specific_competence_name: Demonstrate an understanding of the opportunities available in sports at national and international levels
learning_activity_name: Explore opportunities associated with sports at national and international levels (a place of sports for further education and other careers)
sla_assessment_criteria: Opportunities associated with sports at national and international levels are well explored.
sla_teaching_aids: Newspaper|Magazine|Sport documentary videos|Sport sessions in television|Radio
sla_references: TET(2023), SPORT STUDIES SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION FORM V-VI, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Sports offer opportunities for education, careers and national development. Students explore these at both national and international levels.
sla_notes_details: Nationally, sport leads to scholarships and admission to sports schools and colleges (for example Malya Sports College and university degrees in sport), jobs as players, coaches, referees, physical education teachers, sports journalists, physiotherapists, sports managers and administrators. Internationally, athletes join professional clubs, the Olympic, Commonwealth and African Games, and study abroad on sports scholarships. Sport also promotes tourism, health, business through sponsorship and peace and friendship among nations.
sla_notes_illustrations: A talented athlete from a secondary school wins a place at a sports college, becomes a physical education teacher and later coaches the national team, while others become journalists or physiotherapists in the industry.
sla_notes_daily_life: Sport can be a source of income and a career, for example running a gym, selling sports goods or working as a match official.
sla_exercise: Name two careers in sport apart from playing.::Coach and referee (also sports journalist, physiotherapist).||Which international games can Tanzanian athletes join?::The Olympic Games, Commonwealth Games and All-Africa Games.||How can sport support further education?::Through sports scholarships and admission to sports colleges and universities.

main_competence_name: Demonstrate mastery of the relationship between human physiology and performance in sports
specific_competence_name: Demonstrate a basic understanding of the role of human body systems and movements in sports
learning_activity_name: Apply biomechanical principles (laws of motions, force, friction, stability, etc) to enhance performance in physical exercises and selected sports: Athletics (running, throwing and jumping), swimming, football and netball, basketball, table tennis, tennis, volleyball and handball
sla_name: Biomechanical Principles in Physical Exercises and Sports
sla_assessment_criteria: Biomechanical principles to enhance performance in physical exercises and sports are well applied.
sla_references: TET(2023), SPORT STUDIES SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION FORM V-VI, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Biomechanics applies the laws of mechanics to human movement. Applying it helps athletes move efficiently and safely.
sla_notes_details: Newton's first law (inertia) says a body remains at rest or in uniform motion until a force acts, the second law states force equals mass times acceleration (F = ma), and the third law says every action has an equal and opposite reaction. Force is a push or pull, and friction is the resistance between surfaces that provides grip or slows movement. Stability increases with a low centre of gravity, a wide base of support and greater mass. Other principles include levers in the body, projectile motion and angular momentum. These principles are used in athletics (starts, throws, jumps), swimming (streamlining), football, netball, basketball, table tennis, tennis, volleyball and handball.
sla_notes_illustrations: A sprinter pushes backwards against the starting block (action) and the block pushes forwards (reaction), so a strong push and a forward lean produce greater acceleration. A netball defender lowers her centre of gravity and widens her stance to remain stable.
sla_notes_daily_life: Lifting a heavy load safely with bent knees and a straight back uses the same principle of stability and levers.
sla_exercise: State Newton's third law.::Every action has an equal and opposite reaction.||How can an athlete increase stability?::By lowering the centre of gravity and widening the base of support.||Why do running shoes have studs or grip?::To increase friction so the athlete does not slip.

learning_activity_name: Describe principles of training in sports (specificity, overload, progression, variety, recovery, individuality and consistency)
sla_name: Principles of Training in Sports (Advanced Level)
sla_assessment_criteria: Principles of training in sports are well described.
sla_references: TET(2023), SPORT STUDIES SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION FORM V-VI, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: At Form Six the principles of training are explained in more depth for competitive sports. Athletes use them for long-term planning.
sla_notes_details: Specificity, overload, progression, variety, recovery, individuality and consistency are applied to fitness components such as strength, speed, endurance, flexibility, power and agility. Training is divided into periods (preparation, competition and transition) so that the athlete peaks at the right time. Overtraining, detraining and reversibility are explained as results of ignoring the principles. Coaches assess fitness by tests such as the beep test, sit and reach and skinfold measurement and adapt the programme.
sla_notes_illustrations: A volleyball coach plans a 12-week preparation cycle: base fitness in weeks 1-4, strength and power in weeks 5-8, tactics in weeks 9-12 and easy training in the week before the tournament.
sla_notes_daily_life: Anyone who follows a fitness routine can use these principles to reach a goal such as running a 10 km race.
sla_exercise: What is overtraining?::Training too hard with too little recovery, leading to fatigue and reduced performance.||Name two fitness components.::Strength and endurance (or speed, flexibility, agility).||What is the purpose of periodisation?::To organise training so the athlete peaks for competition.

learning_activity_name: Apply principles of training in selected sports: Basketball, table tennis, tennis, volleyball and handball
sla_name: Applying Principles of Training in Basketball, Table Tennis, Tennis, Volleyball and Handball
sla_assessment_criteria: Principles of training in sports are well applied.
sla_teaching_aids: Tape measure|Height stadiometer|Dynamometer|Skinfold caliper|BP machine|Weigh scales|Sit & reach box|Heart rate monitor|Step test box|Thermometer|Sports watch|Cones
sla_references: TET(2023), SPORT STUDIES SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION FORM V-VI, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: The principles are applied by performing skills in a selected sport and using fitness measurements to monitor progress. Students demonstrate the principles in practice.
sla_notes_details: In basketball, dribbling, shooting and defensive slide drills are made harder by adding time and opponents. In table tennis, rally drills develop reaction and specificity, in tennis, serve and footwork drills are repeated, in volleyball, spike and block sessions are progressed by height, and in handball, passing and shooting drills are done at increasing speed. Tests using tape measure, stadiometer, dynamometer, skinfold caliper, BP machine, weighing scale, sit-and-reach box and heart-rate monitor record fitness before and after training.
sla_notes_illustrations: A tennis player measures resting heart rate, follows an eight-week programme of footwork and serve drills, then measures again to see improvement in fitness.
sla_notes_daily_life: Regular school clubs and community teams use these methods to improve performance and keep members healthy.
sla_exercise: Name one instrument used to measure grip strength.::A dynamometer.||How can a volleyball coach apply progression?::By increasing the height of the net or the number of spikes gradually.||Why is heart rate monitored in training?::To check the intensity of exercise and the level of fitness.

learning_activity_name: Perform advanced tactics and drills in selected sports (principles, systems and styles of play)
sla_name: Advanced Tactics and Drills in Basketball, Table Tennis, Tennis, Volleyball and Handball
sla_assessment_criteria: Advanced tactics and drills in selected sports are well performed.
sla_references: TET(2023), SPORT STUDIES SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION FORM V-VI, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Advanced tactics and drills at Form Six involve systems and styles of play in racket and court team sports. Players practise under pressure and in match situations.
sla_notes_details: In basketball, tactics include fast break, zone and player-to-player defence and pick-and-roll. In volleyball, the receive-set-attack system, 5-1 and 6-2 formations and blocking patterns are taught. In handball, attacking systems such as 3-3 and defensive lines like 6-0 are used. In table tennis and tennis, singles and doubles strategies, serve placement and net play are practised. Principles of play, such as maintaining balance, creating space and communication, apply in all. Guided practice with feedback develops decision-making.
sla_notes_illustrations: Volleyball players rehearse a 6-2 rotation: the setter runs a quick set to the outside hitter while the middle blocker closes the gap, and the drill is repeated with a live block.
sla_notes_daily_life: Teamwork and quick decisions gained in these drills are useful in group work and in leadership roles.
sla_exercise: What is a fast break in basketball?::A quick attack after winning the ball before the defence is set.||Name a defensive system in handball.::The 6-0 defence.||Why is communication important in team tactics?::It coordinates players so that they act together.

learning_activity_name: Play by observing rules and regulations governing selected sports: Basketball, table tennis, tennis, volleyball and handball
sla_name: Playing by the Rules of Basketball, Table Tennis, Tennis, Volleyball and Handball
sla_assessment_criteria: Rules and regulations governing selected sports: Basketball, volleyball, handball, table tennis and tennis are well observed.
sla_teaching_aids: Specific sports rules|Regulations|Whistles|Score sheets|Flag|Electronic officiating devices
sla_references: TET(2023), SPORT STUDIES SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION FORM V-VI, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Playing by the rules is necessary for fair competition in each sport. Students form teams, play and give one another feedback.
sla_notes_details: Basketball rules include travelling, double dribble, fouls and the shot clock. Table tennis rules cover the service, let and scoring to 11 points. Tennis rules include the serve, faults, scoring by points, games and sets and the tiebreak. Volleyball rules include rotation, three touches per side, net violations and scoring to 25 points, and handball rules include the three-step rule, goal-area rules and the seven-metre throw. Rules also cover the roles of officials, score sheets, flags and electronic officiating devices.
sla_notes_illustrations: During a volleyball game students note that a team touches the ball four times, and the referee awards a point to the opponents; peers then explain the three-touch rule.
sla_notes_daily_life: Familiarity with rules helps people to officiate school and village matches fairly and respectfully.
sla_exercise: How many touches is a volleyball team allowed on one side?::Three.||What is travelling in basketball?::Moving with the ball without dribbling.||What is a fault in tennis?::A service that does not land in the correct service box or is not delivered correctly.

specific_competence_name: Design and conduct a project in sports
learning_activity_name: Complete and submit for assessment the project initiated in Form Five
sla_name: Completing and Submitting the Sports Project
sla_assessment_criteria: A project is completed and submitted.
sla_teaching_aids: Newspaper|Magazine|Sport documentary videos|Sport sessions in television|Radio
sla_references: TET(2023), SPORT STUDIES SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION FORM V-VI, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Form Six students complete the project started in Form Five and report their findings. The final report is assessed.
sla_notes_details: The report has a title page, introduction, objectives, methodology, findings, conclusions, recommendations and references. Students write in pairs, use tables or charts to present data and explain sports challenges in Tanzania such as inadequate facilities, funding and training.
